data.text: Design at 8853aa3c. Private ZeroizingBuffer (src/send/buffer.rs) owns one fixed Box<[u8]> at a time; its Drop zeroes the whole allocation, and with no reserve or shrink available, Drop is the only release path. Growth and the final fit build a replacement and assign over the old buffer. read_body keeps its growth policy, limit check, 1 MiB preallocation cap and select precedence. Body::Complete(Bytes) is preserved through Bytes::from_owner. Rejected: Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> (a reallocating Vec can release populated storage unwiped). Kept a protected final fit so a returned Bytes still retains exactly its length, as the old shrink_to_fit did; it copies only when capacity differs from length. Inspected resolved sources: bytes 1.12.1 owned vtable (last release drops the owner once; owned_is_unique is false; Vec/BytesMut conversion deep-copies) and zeroize 1.9.1 (volatile write per element). Public items are unchanged; zeroize is private and already in the normal graph through rustls; no Batter dependency added. ADR-010 review recorded in docs/evidence/api-assessments/http.md. Test instrumentation: cfg(test) probe called from the destructor between the wipe and deallocation, reading only live initialized memory. Ablations (Linux, focused lib tests): 13 of 13 protections removed one at a time were caught by the matching tests; restored tree passed. Release-build cost on Linux x86-64: zeroize 0.26 ms/1 MiB, 2.1 ms/8 MiB, 18 ms/64 MiB, synchronous on the releasing thread. Consumer note: Vec::from(bytes) was previously able to reclaim a unique allocation and now always copies, so a caller wrapping that Vec in its own zeroizing owner stays correct at the cost of one extra bounded copy.

Final commit 03076b228ecee20f6947e4f4e9d2c2ac4617438c, PR https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/pull/110. Supersedes the design note above on one point: the protected final fit was removed. A completed body now keeps the allocation it grew into, at most twice its length and never above the limit (unit-tested). One growth step has the same synchronous cost, now disclosed in the deadline limits and on RESERVE: about 56 ms for 64 MiB. Same mechanism as the batter-70qx cleanup fix, on the admission path. runlimit-postgres/src/gcra.rs run_transaction computes one evaluation instant now = max(database sample, every locked shard's observed_at_ms) and UPDATE_WATERMARKS writes it to every shard in the batch. After a clock regression leaves one shard's watermark ahead, a check_all spanning that shard and another evaluates the other shard's keys at the advanced instant (early replenishment) and permanently advances that shard's clock.

Executed evidence (temporary experiment, PostgreSQL 18.6, 2026-11-10, not committed): policy 1 per 60 s; a shard-1 key consumed and then denied alone; shard 0 watermark set to start+120 s. A single check of the shard-1 key was denied (alone=false), but check_all([shard-0 key, shard-1 key]) was allowed (batch=true), and both shard clocks became start+120 s.

Decision needed: keep one batch evaluation instant (documented single-instant batch semantics, memory parity), or evaluate each check at max(sample, its own shard watermark) and persist per-shard watermarks. Without a clock regression the two are identical. Related: batter-ctk7.2 owns GCRA batch preflight/commit shape.

fields.description: Two confirmed deadlocks in runledger-postgres workflow persistence. (A) Job terminal completion takes the workflow_runs row FOR SHARE when releasing a ready dependent (release.rs workflow_run_allows_step_release_tx) and FOR UPDATE later in recompute_workflow_run_status_tx; two disjoint branches completing together both hold FOR SHARE and both request FOR UPDATE (reproduced on PostgreSQL 18: 35 of 40 iterations deadlocked). The worker does not retry, so the reaper re-runs or dead-letters an already-succeeded job. (B) Steps are inserted in builder order with uuidv7 ids and forward references are allowed, so a dependent declared before its prerequisite has a smaller id. Job completion locks prerequisite P then dependents; external completion, append, list-for-update and cancel lock all steps in id order, so the whole-run locker holds D and waits on P while completion holds P and waits on D (reproduced with a gated test). Fix: every multi-step workflow mutation takes the workflow_runs row FOR UPDATE before any workflow_steps row.

data.text: Investigation at 1053293d6a2598683b815af361c33e8c725fd501; no tracked files changed. Confirmed same-family dial starvation with unchanged source included in /tmp/batter-wznf-probe (1/10/20 candidates, 150 ms latency, 1 s shared deadline: success/timeout/timeout). Confirmed well-known NAT64 prefix rejection and Bytes::from_owner try_into_mut refusal. cargo test -p batter-outbound-http --all-features --locked passed on Rust 1.98.1, Linux; no full workspace matrix or production load/cloud tests run. Fresh TCP and HTTP/1-only are explicit experimental scope; repeated hostname resolution uses Tokio blocking pool and a started resolver can outlive exchange timeout. AWS NAT quota allegation is incorrect (55,000 per destination per IPv4 address); Google default 64 ports is minimum allocation, not universal maximum. Waker-less guard is privately coupled to enclosing timer/cancellation polling; no public exchange deadlock established. Kernel transmission limitation is explicit and does not negate prevention of subsequent userspace writes. Wipe covers only owned body allocation, as documented; copies, shared-slice retention, lost mutable reclamation and synchronous costs are real. README 56 ms is a copy-plus-wipe estimate, not measured full exchange or hard bound. HeaderMap is not a copy of the response body, and kernel TLS bytes are ciphertext. Recommended release assessment: measured connection/NAT/DNS capacity and poll latency before promoting this experimental transport; deliberate decisions on pooling/HTTP2, NAT64 filtering and body-storage policy. Sources checked: AWS NAT gateway basics; Google Cloud NAT ports-and-addresses; Tokio AsyncWrite/spawn_blocking docs; bytes owner conversion docs; local resolved Tokio 1.54.1, bytes 1.12.1 and rustls 0.23.46 sources.

fields.description: Audit point 1.2 investigated 2026-11-11 against master 4e57ab62. Confirmed: (1) the admitted context, deadline, batter.http span and completion event all end at response construction, before any body frame is polled (documented, ADR-008); (2) any Panicked/Aborted direct task or requested abort skips the whole CleanupStack (ADR-002, lifecycle.rs:689-698); (3) the two combine: a connection that outlives drain+cancel forces abort of the server wrapper and skips every finalizer. New evidence: a temporary real-socket probe (not committed) showed an ordinary non-streaming handler returning a fixed 64 MiB body to a client that stops reading produces abort_requested=[http], forced_cancellation=true, cleanup skipped UnsafeTaskExit. So the skip is triggerable by any client on any large-response route, not only by streaming handlers. Refuted or overstated: skipped pool close does not strand server sessions once the process exits (EOF ends the backend; only the Terminate frame is missing; not run against a live server); batter-otlp uses service diagnostics because its final snapshot must follow the shutdown report, not to dodge skipping (batter-i3ny); the per-hook task and Arc in cleanup/acquisition.rs are harmless. fields.description: AdmittedRequest::context() returns a Clone OperationContext that a handler can move into a 'static Sse or Body::from_stream; it compiles and the stream then observes an already-cancelled context, with no deadline, no batter.http span or scoped dispatch during body polls, and a completion event whose latency_ms covers only response construction (crates/batter-axum/src/low_level.rs:277-287, observation.rs:84-87,149). The docs say a streaming design needs a distinct owner, but the library offers none, which is the ADR-010 signal: a known-invalid composition compiles on the canonical path. Proposed, unexecuted: a streaming response owner obtained from the admitted request that issues a body-scoped context cancelled by process forced cancellation (plus optional total and idle budgets) and notified of drain, polls and destroys the body under the first-poll dispatch and HTTP span, and emits one body-completion observation (duration, completed/failed/cancelled/dropped). fields.description: One joined finite-task panic or one requested abort skips every finalizer (lifecycle/tasks.rs:325-328, lifecycle.rs:689-698). The stack cannot tell a finalizer that releases exclusivity (lease release, lockfile or socket-path unlink), which must not run while hidden work may continue, from one that only closes the process's own handles (pool close), where skipping buys nothing. AGENTS.md forbids replacing conservative skipping with abort-then-call-it-clean, so this is a decision for the owner, not a repair. Questions: (a) should registration carry a class so own-handle finalizers run under the remaining budget after an unsafe exit while the report stays unsuccessful; (b) does a joined finite-task panic, whose descendants are admitted through the process scope, need the same treatment as a component panic or wrapper abort; (c) how much of this is still worth doing once forced cancellation closes HTTP connections. Proposed and unexecuted.

data.text:
ADR-010 assessment, 2026-11-11.

INVALID-STATE REVIEW of the current canonical path (HttpBoundary + AdmittedRequest) for a handler that returns a streaming body:
1. Request context moved into the body. Compiles and reaches execution; the stream's first nested run returns Interrupted(Cancelled) because admission cancels the scope when the response future finishes (low_level.rs request_admission_inner). Not expressible locally: OperationContext is Clone + 'static by design, every nested operation depends on that, and Body::from_stream requires 'static. So the canonical path needs an owner, not a prohibition.
2. No body owner. A correct consumer must assemble four things itself: a second admission decision, shutdown observation taken from the root's control handle, its own completion record, and nothing at all for dispatch. That is the 'repeated consumer instructions to coordinate cancellation and finalization' signal.
3. The completion event (observation.rs) measures response construction only; failures after headers and stream duration are invisible.
4. Body polls and destruction run on Hyper's connection task, outside with_current_dispatch and the batter.http span.
Since batter-9wig.1 an unowned body can no longer force wrapper abort; it is cut abruptly halfway through the cancel allowance. Graceful ending is still unowned.

BASELINE EVIDENCE (executed, weak): one fresh agent was asked to write an event stream and a chunked export on the canonical path, write-only, not compiled. It avoided the request context, but it had read the guarantees sentence 'a streaming design needs a distinct owner' and the ADR-008 amendment naming this bead, so the trap rate is not measured. What it shows is the hand assembly: it called OperationAdmission::admit_root a second time inside the handler (a second recorded admission for one request that fails if drain races, which it rendered as 503), took ShutdownSignal from supervisor.handle().signal(), wrote its own Drop guard to cancel the owner and log completion with the correlation id, noted there is no stream equivalent of with_current_dispatch, guessed whether an export should stop at drain or at forced cancellation, invented both lifetime bounds, and could not bound concurrent exports because Bulkhead::run does not cover returned streams.

PROPOSED API (unexecuted):
- AdmittedRequest::into_body(self, budget, build: FnOnce(BodyScope) -> impl Stream<Item = Result<Bytes, E>>) -> axum::body::Body. Consumes the admitted request so the handler's own authority ends where the body's begins.
- BodyBudget: validated total and idle bounds, no unbounded default.
- BodyScope: context() is an OperationContext rooted under process forced cancellation with the body's total deadline, minted from the original admission decision (no second readiness read); draining() for streams that choose to end at drain. Whether to end at drain stays application policy and is the one decision the builder must make explicitly.
- The returned body polls and destroys the stream under the first-poll dispatch and the request's span, ends with a body error (visible truncation, never a false final chunk) on total deadline, idle timeout or forced cancellation, and emits exactly one body-completion event: request_id, outcome completed|failed|deadline_exceeded|idle|cancelled|dropped, bytes, duration_ms.
- Core seam: a low-level continuation captured at admission (operation::low_level) so the adapter can mint the body root lazily without consulting readiness again and without a second per-request token for non-streaming requests. It is adapter authority, not consumer API.
- Not covered by this design: upgraded connections, and admission (bulkhead) permits held for a body's lifetime; both need their own review.

TELEMETRY DECISION: additive. 'HTTP response boundary finished' and its fields stay as they are; the owned path adds a second event. No rename of latency_ms, so no hard cut. A body=none|sized|owned|unowned field on the existing event, to make unowned streams visible, is deferred to the implementation bead.

FAILURE SCENARIOS the implementation must test: context escaped from BodyScope after the body is dropped; stream that ignores draining; idle stream past its bound; total deadline during a pending frame; forced cancellation with a pending frame and with a stalled reader (ordering against the 9wig.1 I/O close); client disconnect mid-stream; handler panic after into_body; never-polled body; scoped (non-global) subscriber.

NOT EXECUTED: any evaluation against the proposed API, which does not exist yet. That fresh-agent task moves to the implementation bead's acceptance.

data.text: Fresh-agent evaluation against the implemented API, executed 2026-11-11: same task as the batter-9wig.2 baseline (an event stream and a 10,000-chunk export on the canonical path, write-only, repository read-only). The agent used AdmittedRequest::into_streaming_response for both routes, scope.context().run for each step, scope.shutdown().draining() for the event stream, and wrote no completion code, citing the rustdoc for each. Its 272-line file compiled unchanged against the working tree as a temporary test target (removed afterwards); the baseline needed 406 lines, a second admit_root, a ShutdownSignal from the root's control handle and its own Drop guard. Decisions it still had to make: budget values; ending an indefinite stream before the mandatory total so it is not logged as a WARN deadline_exceeded; where the pause sits relative to run; no per-step deadline (OperationContext::child was not mentioned for streams); no concurrency bound on bodies. Confusions it reported: the README and rustdoc samples differed in their Interrupted arm, the stream's Interrupted arm looked unreachable and it was unclear whose error the peer sees, the step context argument is unused in every example, shutdown still depends on a non-zero cancel allowance the module cannot see, and there is no application hook for body completion. Acted on in docs: BodyBudget and BodyScope::context rustdoc and the README now cover indefinite streams, child step deadlines, who truncates and why to end with an error. Not acted on, recorded as limits: no completion hook, no body concurrency bound, no metric. One sample; it does not measure how often an agent that has not read these docs falls into the unowned composition, which still compiles.

ADR-010 invalid-state review of the new surface, 2026-11-11.
Enforced by types or library-owned execution: (1) a body bound cannot be a raw or unbounded duration: BodyBudget validates a positive total and a positive idle no longer than it (compile_fail and unit test); (2) BodyScope has no public constructor (compile_fail); (3) the admitted request is consumed, so the handler cannot keep using it after handing the body over (compile_fail); (4) no second readiness decision: the body root comes from the private OperationContinuation that only a successful admission creates (compile_fail in core), so a body starting during drain cannot be refused and nothing unadmitted can be continued; (5) the scope's context is cancelled on every ending, including destruction and a panicking builder (tests); (6) both bounds and forced cancellation end the body without the stream's cooperation, checked before every frame (tests incl. an always-ready source); (7) a library-ended body always errors, so it cannot be reported complete (tests, real-socket missing final chunk); (8) polling, the completion event, application destruction and span release all happen under the captured dispatcher (test with a foreign subscriber; the unprotected span release panicked across registries before it was fixed); (9) exactly one completion event, before application destructors, without error contents (tests).
Not expressible locally, recorded as limits: (a) an unowned streaming body still compiles, because OperationContext is Clone and 'static by design and axum accepts any 'static body; (b) a clone of the request context taken before into_streaming_response can still be moved into the stream; (c) whether to end at drain is application policy, so a stream that ignores drain holds the drain allowance until forced cancellation; (d) the bounds are observed only when the transport polls the body, so a peer that stops reading is ended only by the batter-9wig.1 forced close; (e) OperationContinuation is Clone and a lower-level adapter seam: an adapter that kept one could start roots after its request ended, an obligation its rustdoc states. Deliberately not built, pending a consumer need (ADR-014): a completion hook, a body metric, a concurrency bound or admission permit held for a body's lifetime, upgraded-connection ownership, and a visibility field for unowned bodies on the existing completion event.
Deviations from the bead: the entry point is AdmittedRequest::into_streaming_response rather than into_body, because wrapping the built response accepts anything IntoResponse (Sse, headers plus a body) instead of only a byte stream; and the facade demonstration is an /events route and test in the existing http_service example rather than an eleventh example, which keeps the example inventory unchanged.

fields.description: An owned response body's total and idle bounds (batter-9wig.6) are observed only when Hyper polls the body, and Hyper does not poll a body whose peer is not reading. Such a connection is therefore ended only by the forced connection close at shutdown (batter-9wig.1); while the process runs it can hold a body and its resources for as long as TCP keeps the connection. The serving gate in crates/batter-axum/src/serving/forced_close.rs already wraps every accepted connection's I/O and is the natural place for a per-connection write-progress bound, but the policy (how long, whether it is per connection or tied to a body's budget, how it reaches the gate from the body) is undecided. Proposed and unexecuted.

Repairs: (1) the request's observer owns the batter.http span and clears its published copy when it finishes, so a kept AdmittedRequest or extension holds no span; an owned body holds its copy until it ends (span-close timing includes the body, latency_ms unchanged; documented). Follow-up from panel review of PR #114 (review-fix run 334297e2, CONVERGED, uncommitted). Fixed: the forced-close gate stored wakers only on pending transport polls, so a connection Hyper waits on its body alone after ready polls (pipelined bytes buffered, hyper 1.11.1 conn.rs:491-493; or read side closed, conn.rs:434-435) was never woken and the wrapper was aborted. Every I/O poll now records its task before reading the closed flag. The close instant is recomputed when a component moves the abort deadline earlier, via new additive read-only ShutdownSignal::abort_deadline_before. partial_request_head test now asserts forced_cancellation. New tests: pipelined-bytes socket case, gate unit test for a ready last poll, moved-deadline case (multi-thread), core abort_before state test. Hand mutation checks: pending-only registration and a fixed close instant each fail their tests; forced-close suite 20/20. bash scripts/verify.sh passed on Rust 1.98.1 (4755 passed, 0 failed). Not run: hosted CI, macOS, HTTP/2.

Follow-up from panel review of PR #114 (review-fix run 334297e2, CONVERGED, uncommitted). Fixed: an owned body finished by its advertised Content-Length/exact size or by trailers was reported dropped because Hyper drops it without polling for the end (dispatch.rs:391-397, 426-430); it is now completed. The idle bound is now checked before a frame is accepted, so a frame ready only after its wait expired ends the body with idle_timeout. A response Hyper writes without a body (HEAD, 2xx CONNECT, 1xx, 204, 304; hyper role.rs:515-527) takes no advertised length, so its empty body is completed; Admission now records the request method. Third panel review of PR #114 (master 4e57ab62..9bd23242) repaired in review-fix run 49eecf69 (commit mode none, CONVERGED at fingerprint 838afc7e): (1) owned-body truncation is documented as invisible to an HTTP/1.0 peer for a body without a declared length (Hyper 1.11.1 close-delimited framing), pinned by a real-socket HTTP/1.0 test; (2) the advertised length is settled again from the response request admission returns, so a Content-Length added by a handler tuple counts (socket test, short and met); (3) a panicking is_end_stream/size_hint is reported panicked with protected teardown, whether the transport or destruction asked (destruction test); (4) OperationContinuation and admit_root_with_continuation moved to batter_core::lifecycle::low_level (unreleased) and start() refuses after the admitted operation was cancelled or expired (unit tests). Fixes: (1) OwnedBody::inspect runs is_end_stream/size_hint under the captured dispatcher and request span; (2) framing hand-off moved from a response extension to the admission record's FramingSlot, filled only by a started body, so a response rebuilt around the body is settled; (3) the body is owned before its first size_hint, so a panic at the hand-over ends it (cancel, panicked event) before the application body is destroyed. Fifth panel review (Claude+Codex, master 4e57ab62..763a1586) found that Axum 0.8.9 counts a connection finished (drop(close_rx), serve/mod.rs:388-414) before its task destroys the connection future, which after the forced-close gate's I/O error still holds Hyper 1.11.1's in-flight handler future and response body (dispatch.rs:123-141), so cleanup could run beside a slow destructor. Review-fix loop run 4923a604 CONVERGED (commit mode none, uncommitted, 14 files, 5 repair rounds). Fix: private serving/completion.rs make-service wrapper gives each connection's service, response future and response body a token (atomic count); both registration paths await every token's release after Axum's graceful return inside the registered future, so a destructor still running at the abort deadline gets the wrapper aborted and cleanup skipped. Also: a private StopClock seam with a paused-clock unit test proving the close is recomputed exactly when the abort deadline moves earlier, plus the order-fixed real-supervisor test. New tests: slow pending-body destructor on both registration helpers and slow in-flight handler destructor (tests/operational/forced_close/slow_destructor.rs), completion unit tests, paused-clock gate test. Hand-run mutations: no completion wait, body-less tokens, connect-info path without the wait, and no abort_deadline_before arm each failed their case; a removed post-store re-check in the waiter was NOT caught by the cross-thread test (documented). Verification: bash scripts/verify.sh on Rust 1.98.1 passed on the final tree (4778 passed, 0 failed); two independent terminal reviews reported no findings. ADR-008 row amended; guarantees, references/http.md, README, AGENTS guides and CHANGELOG updated. Not run: hosted CI, macOS, HTTP/2.

Owner decision on the accepted-input contract (branch fix/in-process-routing-state-oj37 from origin/master b8747a5e). Reproduced on that base through a real assembled boundary: a whole Extensions map copied from a handled request and sent through InProcessClient::request gives Path<u64> 500 'Expected 1 but got 2' (3 from a nested source), an inherited invalid-UTF-8 record gives 400 on a valid destination path, MatchedPath is concatenated ('/source/{source_id}/plain'), and the inherited ObservationState/OperationalScope suppress the destination's request span and 'HTTP response boundary finished' event entirely (same coupled symptom jkw6.58 saw). Measured facts on Axum 0.8.9: every Router-dispatched map, including one reaching a fallback, carries OriginalUri and a UrlParams record that the public RawPathParams extractor reports (Ok, or InvalidUtf8InPathParam); MatchedNestedPath is only ever written in the same routing step as UrlParams. CONTRACT: request() accepts an arrival-shaped request, one whose extension map carries no Axum routing record (UrlParams via RawPathParams, MatchedPath, NestedPath, OriginalUri). Caller-inserted application extensions such as ConnectInfo stay accepted and untouched. ENFORCEMENT: detect at client entry with public Axum APIs only, before the router or any application code is polled; a routed map is refused whole, nothing is stripped. OUTCOME: signature stays -> Response; the refusal is the sanitized HttpFailure::Internal response carrying a new public marker response extension with no public constructor, plus one static ERROR event, so it cannot be mistaken for a response the boundary built. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: per-record reset (UrlParams and MatchedNestedPath are private, http 1.5.0 Extensions has no iteration or retain; partial stripping of the nameable records would leave a mixed silent-repair/refuse contract); dropping the whole map (deletes application metadata); Result-returning request or a typed fresh-request builder (hard cut across ~150 call sites in 34 files for a rare composition, and a builder would still need name-based filtering of the cloneable public records); upstream reset facility (not available at the pin, worth an upstream issue but not a dependency of this fix). Residual: a map carrying Batter private records but no Axum record can only come from a low_level wrapper around a non-Router service; clearing those at entry stays with the jkw6.58 flags work. Implementation dispatched to Opus 5.5; no commit authorized.

fields.description: batter_runlimit::http::PreparedHttp::in_process returns a TestClient that holds its own prepared Router and dispatches with router.clone().oneshot(request) (crates/batter-runlimit/src/http.rs, TestClient::request). It does not wrap batter_axum::InProcessClient, so it does not inherit the batter-oj37 entry check: a request built from a whole Extensions map that an Axum router already dispatched still reaches the quota boundary with inherited UrlParams, MatchedPath and Batter observation state. batter-oj37 decided the accepted-input contract for the adapter's client (arrival-shaped requests only; refuse whole, sanitized internal failure with the ReusedRoutingState marker) but ruled out a second public entry point in batter-axum, so the check is not shareable as written. Not reproduced through TestClient itself; inferred from the code path and the batter-oj37 reproduction on the same pinned Axum 0.8.9.

data.text: Implemented by Opus 5.5 in the working tree of branch fix/in-process-routing-state-oj37 (base origin/master b8747a5e); uncommitted, no commit authorized. InProcessClient::request now checks MatchedPath, NestedPath, OriginalUri and the RawPathParams record at entry and refuses the whole request with the sanitized HttpFailure::Internal response carrying the new public batter_axum::ReusedRoutingState marker (private field, no constructor) plus one static ERROR event; signature unchanged; nothing stripped. Tests: crates/batter-axum/tests/route_groups/reused_routing.rs and reused_routing_accepted.rs, 11 tests covering captured, nested, invalid-UTF-8, fallback, native nest_service (private nested matched-path record), each record alone, telemetry of a refusal, kept application extensions and ConnectInfo, a boundary-built 500 without the marker, the copy-by-type migration with the destination's route and one completion event, and ordinary nested routing in one dispatch. Negative control by the implementer: with the check disabled all 7 refusal tests fail and the 4 accepted tests pass. Docs, CHANGELOG (behavior change, signature unchanged), references and ADR-010 assessment updated. Correction to the earlier measured fact: a path no pattern matches, e.g. OPTIONS *, reaches the catch-all fallback with OriginalUri only and no path-parameter record; it is still refused through OriginalUri. VERIFICATION (Rust 1.98.1, x86_64 Linux): owner re-ran the 11 new tests (pass), cargo fmt --check (pass), check_file_budget.sh (0 errors, 2 pre-existing-size notices). Implementer reports: cargo test -p batter-axum, clippy and rustdoc -D warnings pass; one full scripts/verify.sh run FAILED (exit 1, 1039s) in the consumers part at runledger-consumer, PostgreSQL container not reachable within 30s on a host at load ~166 with ~65 foreign containers; fmt, budgets, all four Clippy configurations and the workspace, no-default-features and doctests parts had passed before it. Remaining steps were then run individually on the same tree and passed (runlimit, scripts, cargo doc, HTTP smokes, check_package.py, every consumers sub-step, two of them only on retry at lower load). No uninterrupted full verify.sh pass exists. LIMITS: declared_dispatch benchmark not run; hosted CI not run.
